study type: Secondary analysis of a population-based cross-sectional survey
exposure: Mode of birth (unplanned CS, planned CS, instrumental birth, spontaneous vaginal birth)
How long until the mother held her baby
Health of the infant at 3 months
outcome: Satisfaction with care during labour and birth
cohort: The study included 2139 primiparous women with singleton babies from England, UK, who provided information about their mode of birth.
finding: Birth by unplanned caesarean section was associated with poorer maternal adjustment, and instrumental birth was associated with lower maternal satisfaction with labour and birth, with these relationships partially mediated by psychosocial variables.
mod_finding: Unplanned caesarean section was associated with poorer maternal postnatal adjustment, while instrumental birth was linked to lower maternal satisfaction with labour and birth.
